title: ReRAM crossbar sneak-path and selector limits
bottleneck: In dense ReRAM crossbars, current sneaks through unselected cells, corrupting reads and wasting power; fixing it requires a selector device at every cell, but selectors that are fast, enduring, low-leakage, and CMOS-compatible at scale don't exist in production form. Without good selectors, crossbars must stay small or accept heavy read margins.
why_it_blocks: Sneak paths cap crossbar density and size, which caps the efficiency and capacity of ReRAM-based in-memory computing and storage-class memory. The selector is the unglamorous component gating an entire technology class.
current_state: Ovonic threshold switches and other selector candidates show progress in labs and limited products. A production-grade, high-endurance selector at advanced nodes is still missing. Without production-grade selectors, crossbars must stay small or use wasteful biasing schemes, capping both density and energy efficiency at once.
